correctness.rationale: For FO with unary colors and binary oriented edge R, rank-two closed theories are determined by which rank-one pointed one-variable types are realized. On a simple coherently oriented n-cycle (n≥3), the pointed type records the center color, predecessor color, successor color, and the set of colors present among non-neighbors. The undirected pointed type forgets the predecessor/successor order. In any binary circular word, each length-three factor abc and its reversal cba have equal occurrence support: the only non-palindromic cases are 001↔100 and 011↔110, paired at ends of maximal monochromatic runs. Reversed triples remove the same color multiset from global counts, so the far-neighbor support is equal. Therefore every mixed-neighbor undirected pointed profile determines both directed orders, and each homogeneous-neighbor profile determines one; directed rank-one type sets are recoverable, proving rank-two theory equivalence and the finite characteristic-sentence translation. With three named colors opposite orientations of the 012 triangle have identical undirected reducts but ∃x∃y(P0(x)∧P1(y)∧R(x,y)) differs. Independent enumeration of 8,184 binary words at cycle lengths 3 through 12 confirmed erasure recovery, plus sharp ternary witness. These bounded checks are not the all-length proof.

value.rationale: Changing from directed successors to unoriented adjacency is a natural expressive-power reduction. The exact preservation of all FO rank-two sentence theories for the binary-color class, its constructive characteristic-sentence consequence, and the sharp ternary counterexample isolate a useful boundary distinct from counting equivalence classes of words or graphs.
